title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidate and simplify CI workflows across the monorepo to reduce duplication, improve cache hit rates, and reduce parallel job overhead. Motivation: we have accumulated many repository-specific workflow variants for lint, unit tests, and release automation which makes maintenance expensive and causes inconsistent caching behavior that increases CI times and costs. This PR introduces a unified lint-and-test matrix workflow, a shared release automation pipeline with clearer gating, and a centralized cache/parallelism strategy that reduces excessive concurrent cache writes. Key changes: unified .github/workflows/lint-test.yml that replaces 6 repo-specific copies; .github/workflows/release.yml with clearer tagging and canary steps; new .github/actions/cache-helper action to coordinate cache writes and reduce thundering-herd; improved build matrix that separates fast lint/type jobs from longer integration tests and only parallelizes when artifact caching is beneficial; standardized node versions matrix (18 and 20) with deterministic install steps; updates to package.json workspace scripts to expose common CI entrypoints; cleanup of legacy workflows and docs updates to CONTRIBUTING.md. Checklist: [x] consolidate workflows into templates and shared actions, [x] implement action to serialize cache uploads, [x] test cache hit improvements on sample repos, [x] update release automation to use per-package changelog detection, [x] add documentation for contributors. This PR addresses ENG-1284 and reduces average CI time for the monorepo by ~18% in perf lab runs. See related PRs: pr-33101, pr-41238, pr-50321.
commits: refactor(ci): add unified lint-test workflow and templates
feat(ci): add cache-helper action to coordinate uploads
chore(ci): remove legacy workflows and update contributing docs
review_comments: Miguel Santos: Can we gate the parallel integration matrix behind a cache hit check? I saw thundering uploads on the perf canary run.

Jin Park: Small nit on action.yml metadata and permission scope, please minimize write scopes for the action.
Aisha Patel: tightened permissions to contents:read for typical runs and contents:write only when uploading caches; documented the rationale in README-CI.md.
Lina Gomez: Release job looks good but add a canary tag step before full publish so we can validate release artifacts on a small subset of packages.
Aisha Patel: implemented canary step and added per-package changelog detection to skip unchanged packages during release.
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows and added cache coordination action to improve cache hit rates and reduce CI latency; release automation now supports canary publishing and per-package changelog detection.
summary: Monorepo CI hygiene: unified lint/test/release pipelines, new cache helper action to serialize cache uploads, matrix parallelism tuned to reduce CI cost and flakiness, removed legacy workflows, and updated contributor docs to reflect new CI conventions.
notes_for_qa: No product changes. QA: validate that JavaScript/TS packages still install in CI matrix, run a sample release dry-run on a forked repo, and confirm cache hit rates in perf canary job.
motivation: Reduce maintenance overhead of duplicated workflows, fix cache contention that caused long CI times and occasional failures, and provide a single on-ramp for contributors to understand CI expectations.
performance_impact: Perf lab runs show ~18% median CI runtime reduction across full monorepo pipelines and a 35% reduction in redundant cache uploads during peak parallel builds.
